findings.reason: The protected SQL solution computes final bank account balances by projecting transactions as signed changes (-amount for paid_by, +amount for paid_to) using UNION ALL, grouping by user_id to sum net changes, and performing a LEFT JOIN with the Users table. It adds starting credit to COALESCE(net_change, 0) and sets credit_limit_breached to 'Yes' if final credit < 0 and 'No' otherwise. The query runs in O(N log N) time and O(N) space; no candidate is required.

Using UNION ALL ensures duplicate transfers are preserved. LEFT JOIN to Users retains users with no transactions, and COALESCE handles null aggregate sums correctly. CASE expression strictly checks final credit < 0 for breach status.
UNION ALL creates 2t signed rows. Grouping, joining, and sorting N total rows takes O(N log N) upper bound time and O(N) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts Users and Transactions tables and returns columns user_id, user_name, credit, and credit_limit_breached.

The approach accurately details signed balance change projection via UNION ALL, net change aggregation, LEFT JOIN user retention, COALESCE default handling, CASE breach logic, and O(N log N) time / O(N) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover two separate aggregate joins, correlated subquery overhead, inner join pitfalls, zero balance non-breaches, one-sided transaction histories, multiple transfer retention, transaction date independence, UNION deduplication traps, and non-unique user names.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the identical UNION ALL LEFT JOIN balance aggregation query with SHA-256 digest e2b4aac70ee47f0406de27dc5dd1f0cdff48231dc71d9944af5b43e0c2dcf5b5. Verified submission remains untouched.

Statement structure and factual evidence confirmed Users and Transactions interface, three examples, three constraints, and 3 local tables. Bound to content SHA-256 f664f3fcf4447d4c2472c9e017471858bb4799b05c7420a91fd1e917f71df270.
